title: Where it grows
subtitle: Jerez and the Canaries
objectives: Name other places that grow it

steps.title: Jerez
steps.body: Palomino is about 95% of the vineyards of Jerez, in Andalusia, around Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María and Sanlúcar de Barrameda, the Sherry triangle. The climate is hot, with over 300 sunny days a year, and two winds: the humid Poniente from the Atlantic and the hot, dry Levante from the east.

steps.title: Albariza
steps.body: The best vineyards are on albariza, a brilliant white soil with up to 40% chalk, formed from marine diatoms. It absorbs winter rain like a sponge and holds it for the dry summer, then forms a hard crust that reduces evaporation. Its white surface reflects sunlight. Pagos, named vineyard areas, like Macharnudo and Carrascal, sit on albariza.

steps.explanation: Jerez has its own vocabulary of land and wind.

steps.title: Elsewhere
steps.body: Palomino is also grown in the Canary Islands, as Listán Blanco, where it makes dry table wines on volcanic soil. Galicia, South Africa, Australia and California grow some, once for fortified wines. Today, a few Jerez producers make unfortified Palomino table wines, showing the albariza in a new way.

steps.prompt: What is special about albariza soil?
options: It stores winter rain for summer
steps.explanation: Its chalky structure holds water deep for the dry summer.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Albariza stores water and reflects sun
It's Listán Blanco in the Canaries
